brief: Weekly chart roundup from Syz. Microsoft suffered a global outage Friday affecting multiple regions except China, which runs separate infrastructure. Nvidia's CEO resigned amid an ongoing investigation; the stock has fallen 36% from its all-time high, wiping over $2tn in market value, marking a sixth straight weekly decline and its lowest price since July 2025, and handing the title of world's largest company back to Apple. Despite the slide, Nvidia now trades near 10x forward earnings, cheaper than Broadcom (17x), TSMC (18x), Alphabet (19x) and AMD (33x); only Micron is cheaper at 4.3x. Goldman expects Nvidia to honor existing AI financing commitments, but whether new deals hold the same terms is an open question, with neocloud borrowing costs in focus as CCC credit spreads sit near cycle-wide highs; Nvidia's Tuesday Q3 report, and any comment on its $500bn in commitments, is framed as the next signal. Vanguard and BlackRock hold Nvidia's largest reported blocks; Jensen Huang holds a 3.41% stake. SpaceX's connectivity revenue grew 69.5% y/y in Q3, far outpacing AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon, as it moves toward mobile spectrum. Binance says it has fully covered its $6.3bn hack with a new proof-of-reserves snapshot.
